hits.snippet: Dec 3 \(Reuters\) – Verkada was valued at $5\.8 billion in its latest investment round led by CapitalG, more than a billion dollars higher than its previous round in February, the AI-based security products maker said on Wednesday\. The company provides cloud-managed video security cameras, access control, environmental sensors, alarms, workplace tools and intercoms to organizations across 171 countries\. Moonshot AI, the Beijing-based startup behind the Kimi chatbot series, has raised approximately $3\.5B in its most recent financing round, cementing its place among the best-funded AI companies to emerge from China in recent years\. The company’s largest single raise was a roughly $2B Series D completed in May 2026, led by Meituan’s venture capital arm\. That round valued Moonshot at $20B post-money, a number that would have seemed absurd not long ago for a company founded in 2023\. ## From $300M to $20B in three years Moonshot launched with an initial valuation of around $300M\. The firm, which has backed artificial intelligence companies including Anthropic, Cursor and Perplexity, has raised four separate funds dedicated to backing young startups in a moment when the AI race is upending the fundraising market\. # Singapore start-up Ropedia raises US$22 mil in pre-Series A round for robot-training data The robotics data company has raised US$30 million so far, and will use the latest funds to gather more training data, increase device production and expand in Singapore and the US\. Ropedia, a Singapore start-up that supplies training data for robots and physical artificial intelligence systems, has raised US$22 million \($28\.4 million\) in a pre-Series A funding round\. It did not identify the investors in the latest round, saying only that it was led by venture firms with experience in AI, deep technology and infrastructure in Southeast Asia\. The deal brings its total funding to US$30 million\. An earlier round included investors and individuals connected to Google, Andreessen Horowitz, Nvidia and Amazon, according to the company\. Ropedia's proprietary wearable devices record first-person video, depth, movement and audio as people carry out physical tasks\. The company processes that information into training material for developers seeking to teach robots how to perform tasks in real-world settings\. # Robotics startup Generalist AI is in talks to raise a new funding round at a $3 billion valuation Venture firm 8VC is expected to lead the round, according to people familiar with the discussions\. The round is in progress, and details could change\. Generalist AI and 8VC did not respond to requests for comment\. It's the latest example of investors pouring money into physical AI AI systems that can act in the real world\. Generalist is competing with startups like Physical Intelligence, valued at more than $11 billion, Skild AI, valued at more than $14 billion, Field AI, valued at $2 billion, and Genesis AI, which is in talks to raise funding at a $3 billion valuation\. The fresh funding comes just one month after Generalist announced it had raised $400 million to develop more sophisticated AI models for robots\. That round valued the company at $2 billion and was led by Radical Ventures, with participation from 8VC, Union Square Ventures, Nvidia, and Bezos Expeditions\. Generalist was founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind robotics researchers Pete Florence and Andy Zeng and former Boston Dynamics roboticist Andrew Barry\. # China’s Moonshot AI in talks on pre-IPO funds at US$50 billion value This should mark the final infusion of capital for Moonshot before an IPO as soon as 2026 Published Wed, Jul 22, 2026 · 10:18 AM MOONSHOT AI is preparing to begin discussions in August on a final round of fundraising before listing in Hong Kong, capitalising on the excitement around its latest model to raise capital at a valuation of as much as US$50 billion\. The Chinese AI lab should close in coming days a financing round that began in summer 2026 at a valuation of US$31\.5 billion, people familiar with the matter said\. Once finalised, Moonshot then intends to immediately open discussions with potential backers about a follow-on capital-raising, the people said, asking to remain unidentified to talk about a private deal\. That should mark the final infusion of capital for Moonshot before an initial public offering as soon as 2026\. The speed with which Moonshot is tapping capital markets underscores investor interest in a startup that has upended perceptions of how far Chinese artificial intelligence technology lags American\.
